title: Cost Sculptor: per-tenant regional allocator with tiered fallbacks and exposure limits
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Implement a tenant-scoped regional allocation service ("Cost Sculptor") that limits a tenant's short-term exposure while maximizing use of lower-cost instance classes. The feature combines: (1) a per-tenant exposure cap (soft cap) over a sliding window, (2) a probabilistic preference model to rank candidate regions and GPU classes by cost, SLO risk, and preemption likelihood, and (3) a progressive fallback chain that degrades through spot preemptible -> mixed-instance GPU pool -> smaller model-variant before using on-demand guaranteed capacity when necessary.
acceptance_criteria: Configurable soft exposure cap per tenant expressed in USD per 1h/24h windows
Routing chooses cheaper region/GPU class while keeping 95th-percentile latency within SLO for P0 routes < 150ms increase
Progressive fallback chain triggers automatically when exposure cap is near exhaustion and logs the exact fallback decision and reason
Metrics emitted: tenant_exposure_usd, route_rank_score, fallback_triggered, eviction_risk_score
E2E tests that simulate sustained traffic and preemption events to validate graceful degradation and no billing spikes
proposal_summary: Introduce a lightweight decision service adjunct to the existing router that maintains per-tenant sliding-window spend estimates and computes a composite score for each candidate allocation (region, tier, GPU class, model variant). Score = alpha * normalized_cost + beta * latency_risk + gamma * eviction_risk + delta * affinity_penalty. When a tenant's exposure approaches their soft cap, bias scoring towards lower-exposure routes and activate progressive degradation policies. The service publishes decisions and enough context to reproduce routing (for audits and rollouts).
implementation_notes: New component: cost-sculptor-service (K8s deployment, stateless w/ Redis-backed sliding window counts)
Sliding window uses 5m buckets aggregated to 1h and 24h views. Store USD-equivalent token costs using current price map + instance-hour amortization for ongoing allocations
Routing changes: router queries cost-sculptor with candidate set; cost-sculptor returns top-N ranked allocations and a 'conservatism' flag indicating whether to prefer guaranteed capacity
Add eviction risk model: light-weight heuristic using current spot eviction rate by region/sku + tenant historical preemption sensitivity
Model-variant degradation: extend model catalog metadata with 'degradation_chain' and quality impact estimate (Q-loss metric) to allow safe size/precision fallbacks
Telemetry: instrument route decision traces, add tenant_exposure_usd and chosen_candidate tags to existing tracing pipeline
API: tenant profile config endpoint to set soft caps, enable/disable progressive fallback, and set conservatism thresholds
rollout_plan: Phase 0 - feature flag locked to internal tenants: deploy cost-sculptor-service behind ff_cost_sculptor
Phase 1 - opt-in beta: enable for 5 customers with varied workloads for 2 weeks, gather cost/latency/regression metrics
Phase 2 - controlled ramp: enable for 20% of traffic across multi-tenant groups, monitor eviction and billing anomalies
Phase 3 - GA: expose config in Console, default soft cap off but recommended for new tenants; ship runtime-1.22
risks: Incorrect cost mapping could bias routing to overly aggressive preemptible use leading to client-visible regressions
Sliding window staleness during controller restarts could allow temporary overspend spikes; mitigated by bounded reconciliation and safety limits
Complexity: added failure modes between router and cost-sculptor-service; fallback to router-only decision-making required
Tenant confusion if automatic degradation happens without clear console signals — need UX/notifications
testing_steps: Unit tests for score calculation with mocked cost/latency/eviction inputs
Integration test: router + cost-sculptor with simulated candidate pools and deterministic eviction events
Chaos test: kill Redis and restart cost-sculptor to validate safe fallback and no overspend beyond emergency cap
Load test: run steady-state traffic at 2x typical tenant throughput for 6 hours to verify sliding window accounting and latency SLOs
Canary: enable for a single low-impact tenant during a business day with SRE on-call monitoring
